answer: Each agent registers by locking 10GB of unique, address-mapped RAM to a willow smart contract that monitors delta variations in high-frequency access patterns. A velvet memory controller locks each physical sector to a singular agent process, preventing the sharing of underlying registers between identities. A verifier audits the address-bound memory state during random intervals; failing the delta check results in immediate revocation. Adding 1,000 identities requires 10TB of dedicated, non-virtualized physical memory access, preventing pooling since hardware capacity cannot be cloned.
